title: Rehmat Medical Centre - Hospital Overview and Contact Information
content: Rehmat Medical Centre (RMC) is a 250-bed multi-specialty private hospital in Islamabad, Pakistan. Address: Main Service Road, Sector G-10, Islamabad. Main helpline and appointments: 051-111-555-000 (7:00 AM to 10:00 PM daily). Emergency department direct line: 051-111-555-911 (24 hours). WhatsApp appointments: 0300-0000000. Email: appointments@rehmatmedical.example. OPD hours: Monday to Saturday, 9:00 AM to 9:00 PM. Sunday: OPD closed, emergency, laboratory collection (8:00 AM to 2:00 PM) and pharmacy remain open. The emergency department, in-patient wards, ICU and main pharmacy operate 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Staff can assist in English and Urdu; Punjabi and Pashto-speaking staff are available at the reception on request.

title: Visiting Hours and Visitor Policy
content: General ward visiting hours are 4:00 PM to 6:00 PM and 7:00 PM to 8:00 PM daily. Only two visitors are allowed at a time per patient, and each patient is issued one attendant pass that allows stay beyond visiting hours. Private rooms: visiting is allowed from 11:00 AM to 8:00 PM, with one attendant permitted overnight. ICU, CCU and NICU: visiting is limited to 15 minutes, twice daily (12:00 PM and 6:00 PM), one visitor at a time, and visitors must wear the provided gown and sanitize hands. Children under 12 are not allowed in ICU or general wards unless the patient is a parent or sibling and the nurse in charge gives permission. Visitors with fever, cough, or other infectious symptoms must not enter patient areas. Visitor passes must be collected from the main reception against a CNIC. Flowers and outside food for patients on a restricted diet are not allowed; check with the nurse in charge first.

title: How to Book an Appointment
content: Patients can book an OPD appointment in four ways: (1) the hospital chatbot or website, (2) calling the helpline 051-111-555-000, (3) WhatsApp message to the appointments number, or (4) visiting the OPD reception in person. Information needed to book: patient full name, age, mobile number, CNIC (or B-Form for children under 18), preferred department or doctor, and preferred date and time. New patients receive a Medical Record (MR) number after the first booking; returning patients should provide their MR number to speed up booking. Appointments are confirmed by SMS and WhatsApp with the doctor name, date, time slot, room number, and token number. Slots are 15 minutes for follow-up visits and 20 to 30 minutes for new patient consultations. Patients should arrive 15 minutes early for registration and vitals. Same-day appointments depend on availability; walk-in patients are seen after scheduled patients. Appointments for minors must be booked by a parent or legal guardian.

title: Rescheduling, Cancellation and No-Show Policy (Current - Effective 1 January 2026)
content: This policy replaces all earlier cancellation policies. Rescheduling or cancelling: patients may reschedule or cancel free of charge up to 12 hours before the appointment time via the helpline, WhatsApp, chatbot or at reception. Late cancellation: cancelling less than 12 hours before the appointment incurs a fee of 20 percent of the consultation fee, which is deducted from any advance payment or added to the next visit. No-show: if the patient does not attend without informing the hospital, 20 percent of the consultation fee is charged. Repeat no-shows: after two no-shows within 90 days, the patient must pay the full consultation fee in advance for future bookings. Late arrival: patients arriving more than 15 minutes after their slot may be moved to the end of the doctor's list or asked to rebook, depending on the doctor's schedule. Doctor-initiated changes: if the hospital or doctor cancels, the patient is offered a new slot or a full refund of any advance payment with no fee. Emergencies, hospital admissions, and documented medical emergencies are exempt from late cancellation and no-show charges.

title: Rescheduling and Cancellation Policy (SUPERSEDED - Valid 2024 to 31 December 2025)
content: NOTE: This version of the policy is OUTDATED and was replaced on 1 January 2026. It is kept for audit and reference only. Under the 2024 policy, patients had to cancel at least 24 hours before an appointment to avoid charges. Cancellations within 24 hours were charged 50 percent of the consultation fee. A no-show was charged the full consultation fee. After three no-shows, the patient's online booking access was suspended for 30 days. Patients arriving more than 30 minutes late lost their appointment. For the current cancellation rules, refer to the policy effective 1 January 2026.

title: Emergency Services vs Routine OPD - When to Go Where
content: The Emergency Department (ED) is open 24 hours and treats life-threatening or urgent conditions. Go to the ED or call 051-111-555-911 for: chest pain or pressure, difficulty breathing, signs of stroke (face drooping, arm weakness, slurred speech), severe bleeding, serious road accidents or burns, loss of consciousness, seizures, severe allergic reaction, poisoning, high fever with confusion, pregnancy-related bleeding or severe pain, and sudden severe abdominal pain. Do not book an OPD appointment for these situations. For ambulance service in Pakistan, you can also call Rescue 1122 where available or Edhi 115. Routine OPD is for non-urgent problems such as follow-ups, chronic condition reviews, mild fever, skin problems, check-ups, and vaccinations. Emergency patients are triaged by severity, not arrival time, so a stable patient may wait longer than a critical one. The hospital chatbot cannot give medical diagnosis; for any symptoms that seem serious, patients should go to the emergency department immediately.

title: Departments and Services Overview
content: Rehmat Medical Centre departments: Cardiology, Orthopedics and Sports Medicine, Gynecology and Obstetrics, Pediatrics and Neonatology, General Medicine, General Surgery, ENT, Ophthalmology, Dermatology, Urology, Gastroenterology and Hepatology, Neurology, Pulmonology, Endocrinology and Diabetes, Psychiatry and Counselling, Dentistry, Physiotherapy and Rehabilitation, Nutrition and Dietetics. Diagnostic services: 24-hour laboratory, digital X-ray, ultrasound, CT scan, MRI (1.5 Tesla), ECG, echocardiography, treadmill stress test, endoscopy and colonoscopy, and bone density scan. Other services: 24-hour pharmacy, ambulance, blood bank, day-care procedures, executive health check-up packages, vaccination clinic, and online video consultation. Specialist OPD days vary by doctor; use the doctor directory or ask the booking assistant for current availability.

title: Consultation Fees and Payment Methods
content: Consultation fees depend on the doctor's grade: General Physician or Medical Officer from PKR 1,500 to 2,000; Consultant from PKR 3,000 to 4,500; Senior Consultant or Professor from PKR 5,000 to 7,000. Exact fees for each doctor are listed in the doctor directory. Follow-up visits with the same doctor within 14 days of the first visit, for the same complaint, are charged at 50 percent of the fee. Online video consultation fees are 20 percent lower than in-person fees. Accepted payment methods: cash (PKR), debit and credit cards (Visa, Mastercard, UnionPay), bank transfer, JazzCash, Easypaisa, Raast QR, and cheques only for corporate panel accounts. Receipts are issued at the cashier counter and sent by SMS or email on request. Charges for laboratory tests, imaging, procedures and room rent are separate from consultation fees. Fees are subject to revision; the amount shown at booking time applies to that appointment.

title: Health Insurance, Panel Companies and Sehat Card
content: The hospital has cashless panel arrangements with several private health insurers and corporate clients, and accepts the Sehat Card Plus for eligible in-patient treatment. Panel insurers (sample list, verify at the insurance desk): Jubilee Health Insurance, EFU Health Insurance, Adamjee Insurance, and State Life group health plans. To use insurance: bring your insurance card and original CNIC; the Insurance Desk (ground floor, near the main reception, open 9:00 AM to 8:00 PM) verifies eligibility and obtains pre-authorization. Planned admissions and procedures require pre-authorization from the insurer, usually 24 to 48 hours in advance. OPD consultations and lab tests are covered only if your specific plan includes outpatient benefits. Items commonly excluded: cosmetic procedures, dental cosmetics, certain pre-existing conditions during waiting periods, and non-medical items such as toiletries. If the insurer rejects a claim, the patient is responsible for the balance. For Sehat Card Plus, coverage is limited to listed in-patient packages for eligible families; eligibility is verified with CNIC at the Sehat Card help desk. The chatbot cannot confirm coverage for a specific patient; please contact the Insurance Desk.

title: Refund Policy
content: Appointment refunds: if the hospital or doctor cancels an appointment, the full advance payment is refunded. If the patient cancels at least 12 hours before the appointment, a full refund is given; cancellations within 12 hours are refunded minus the 20 percent late cancellation fee. Laboratory tests: refunds are possible only before the sample is collected. Imaging: refunds are possible only before the scan is started. Procedures and packages: refunds depend on the package terms and are reviewed by the Billing Department. Refund processing time: cash refunds are issued at the cashier counter with the original receipt; card, JazzCash, Easypaisa and bank refunds are processed to the original payment method within 7 to 10 working days. Consultation fees are not refunded after the consultation has taken place. Refund requests can be made at billing@rehmatmedical.example or at the billing counter with the receipt and CNIC.

title: Laboratory Tests - Fasting and Preparation Guide
content: Laboratory sample collection: Monday to Saturday 7:00 AM to 9:00 PM, Sunday 8:00 AM to 2:00 PM. Home sample collection is available in selected areas of Islamabad and Rawalpindi on request, with an extra service charge. Fasting tests: fasting blood glucose, lipid profile (cholesterol), and some other tests typically require 8 to 10 hours of fasting. Water is allowed and encouraged during fasting. Do not eat, drink tea, coffee or juice, or chew gum during the fast. Non-fasting tests: CBC (complete blood count), HbA1c, thyroid profile (TSH), liver function tests (LFTs) and kidney function tests usually do not require fasting, but follow the instructions given by your doctor. Medications: continue your regular medicines unless your doctor has told you to stop them; for diabetes medicines on the day of a fasting test, consult your doctor. Please bring the doctor's prescription or test request and your CNIC. Normal turnaround times: CBC and basic chemistry same day within a few hours; cultures 48 to 72 hours; specialized tests several days. Results are available from the Reports Counter or through the patient portal. During Ramadan, ask the lab about fasting-related timing.

title: MRI Scan Preparation
content: Before an MRI: arrive 30 minutes early for registration and a safety questionnaire. Remove all metal items including jewellery, watches, hairpins, belts, coins, keys, hearing aids, and dentures with metal parts. Clothing with metal zippers or embroidery may need to be changed into a hospital gown. Inform the radiology staff BEFORE the scan if you have a pacemaker, cochlear implant, aneurysm clip, metal implants or plates, insulin pump, or any metal fragments in the body, or if you are pregnant or may be pregnant. Tell staff if you are claustrophobic; the technician can explain options. Eating and drinking: for most MRI scans there is no restriction; for abdominal or contrast scans you may be asked to fast for 4 to 6 hours. If contrast dye is needed, a recent kidney function test (creatinine) may be required. The scan takes 20 to 60 minutes depending on the area; you must stay still during the scan. The report is usually ready in 24 to 48 hours. Final instructions are given by the radiology department when the scan is booked.

title: Ultrasound Preparation Guide
content: Abdominal ultrasound (liver, gallbladder, pancreas, spleen): fast for 6 to 8 hours before the scan; water is allowed in small sips. Pelvic or obstetric ultrasound in early pregnancy and pelvic scans for men and women: a full bladder is required. Drink 4 glasses (about 1 litre) of water starting 1 hour before the scan and do not urinate until the scan is done. KUB (kidneys, ureters, bladder) ultrasound: a moderately full bladder is needed. Later pregnancy ultrasounds: usually no special preparation; follow your gynecologist's instructions. Thyroid, breast, and soft tissue ultrasounds: no preparation required. Wear loose, comfortable clothing and bring previous scan reports and the doctor's referral. Pregnancy anomaly scans and other detailed scans require an appointment. Ultrasound reports are typically available the same day.

title: Endoscopy and Colonoscopy Preparation
content: Upper GI endoscopy: do not eat or drink for 6 to 8 hours before the procedure. Inform the doctor about blood thinners, aspirin, diabetes medicines, and allergies. Colonoscopy: requires bowel preparation. The Gastroenterology department provides a written prep sheet when the procedure is booked, which usually includes a low-fibre or clear liquid diet the day before and a prescribed laxative solution taken the evening before or the morning of the procedure. Follow the prep sheet exactly; poor preparation can lead to an incomplete examination and the need to repeat the procedure. Both procedures may be done under sedation, so the patient must have an adult escort to take them home, and should not drive, sign legal documents, or operate machinery for 24 hours afterward. Do not stop blood thinners or other regular medicines on your own; the gastroenterologist will advise you. Wear loose clothing, bring your CNIC and previous reports, and arrive 1 hour before the scheduled time. Day-care admission is required and the procedure takes 15 to 45 minutes.

title: What to Bring for Your First Visit
content: For a first visit, please bring: original CNIC (or B-Form for children, and parent CNIC); the appointment confirmation SMS or WhatsApp message; previous medical records, prescriptions, lab reports, X-rays or scan films and discharge summaries related to the problem; a list of all medicines you currently take, including herbal medicines and supplements; your insurance card or Sehat Card if applicable; and payment method for the consultation fee. For children: vaccination card and growth records. For pregnant patients: previous antenatal records and scan reports. Arrive 15 minutes early for registration, where you will receive your MR number, and vitals (blood pressure, temperature, weight) will be checked by the nurse. Please wear a mask if you have cough or fever. Mobile phones should be on silent mode in consultation rooms.

title: Medical Records and Report Collection
content: Lab and radiology reports can be collected from the Reports Counter (ground floor) from 9:00 AM to 8:00 PM, or accessed through the patient portal using your MR number and registered mobile number. A collection slip or SMS with the report ready date is given at the time of the test. Reports not collected within 30 days are archived and can be requested from Medical Records. Radiology films and CD copies are issued on request; extra copies may incur a charge. Discharge summaries and medical records: to request your own records, submit a written request at the Medical Records Department with your original CNIC and MR number. Records are normally issued within 3 to 5 working days. A representative can collect records only with a signed authorization letter and copies of both CNICs. Records of minors can be released to a parent or guardian. Medical records are confidential and are not shared with employers, relatives, or third parties without patient consent, except where required by law or a court order.

title: Online Video Consultation (Telemedicine) Guide
content: Video consultations are available for follow-up visits, report review, chronic disease management, and minor non-urgent problems with selected doctors. Not suitable for: emergencies, new complaints needing physical examination, chest pain, breathing difficulty, or injuries. Booking: select 'Online Consultation' while booking through the chatbot, website, or helpline; payment is required in advance via card, JazzCash, Easypaisa, or Raast QR. A video link is sent by SMS and WhatsApp 15 minutes before the appointment. Requirements: a smartphone or computer with a stable internet connection, camera and microphone, and a quiet, well-lit place. Keep previous reports and medicines ready. Online consultation fees are 20 percent lower than in-person fees. After the consultation, the e-prescription is sent through the patient portal and WhatsApp. If the doctor feels an in-person exam is needed, the doctor will advise and you will be given a priority in-person slot. Technical failures on the hospital side are rescheduled or refunded in full.

title: Directions, Parking and Accessibility
content: Location: Main Service Road, Sector G-10, Islamabad. The hospital is a few minutes from the nearest main road junction and has a covered main entrance and a separate emergency entrance on the east side. Parking: free parking for patients and visitors in the basement and ground-level lot for the first 2 hours; Rs. 50 per hour after that. Reserved parking is available for patients with disabilities and for ambulances. Motorcycle parking is at the north side. Public transport and ride-hailing apps (Careem, inDrive, Bykea) can drop off at the main gate or the emergency entrance. Accessibility: wheelchair ramps at all entrances, elevators to all floors, wheelchair-accessible washrooms, and free wheelchairs and stretchers available at the main entrance and emergency. Staff assistance for elderly patients can be requested at the reception. Prayer rooms are on the ground floor for men and women. A cafeteria and a pharmacy are located on the ground floor.

title: Ramadan and Public Holiday Timings
content: During Ramadan, OPD timings are adjusted: OPD runs from 10:00 AM to 3:00 PM and again from 8:30 PM to 11:30 PM, Monday to Saturday. Laboratory collection runs from 8:00 AM to 2:00 PM and 8:30 PM to 11:00 PM. Emergency, in-patient wards, ICU and pharmacy remain open 24 hours. Appointments for specific doctors may have different Ramadan schedules, so please confirm at booking. Public holidays: on Eid-ul-Fitr, Eid-ul-Adha, Ashura (9th and 10th Muharram), Independence Day (14 August) and Pakistan Day (23 March), routine OPD is closed unless announced otherwise; emergency, in-patient care and pharmacy remain open. Friday: OPD is open, with a short break for Jummah prayers from 1:00 PM to 2:00 PM. Holiday schedules are announced on the hospital website and social media pages at least 3 days in advance.

title: Patient Privacy and Data Protection Policy
content: Rehmat Medical Centre treats all patient information as confidential. Personal data collected (name, CNIC, contact details, medical history, test results) is used only for treatment, billing, appointment management, and legal requirements. Data is not sold or shared with third parties for marketing. Insurance companies receive only the information required for claims, with patient consent. Patients have the right to access their records, request corrections, and ask how their information is used. The AI booking assistant does not give medical diagnosis, does not store sensitive medical details beyond what is needed for the booking, and will not disclose appointment or medical information of one person to another person without verification. Verification may be needed using MR number, CNIC last digits and registered mobile number. Concerns about privacy can be sent to privacy@rehmatmedical.example. Staff access to records is role-based and logged.

title: Cardiology Department
content: The Cardiology department diagnoses and treats heart and blood vessel conditions. Services: consultation for chest pain, palpitations, high blood pressure, breathlessness and heart failure; ECG; echocardiography; treadmill stress test (TMT); 24-hour Holter monitoring; 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring; angiography and angioplasty in the cardiac cath lab; pacemaker follow-up; cardiac rehabilitation; and preventive heart health check-ups. Cardiology OPD runs Monday to Saturday; individual doctor days are listed in the directory. Patients should bring previous ECGs, echo reports, and a list of medicines. For a treadmill test, wear comfortable shoes and clothing and avoid a heavy meal 2 hours before. Chest pain that is severe, spreading to the arm or jaw, or associated with sweating or breathlessness is an emergency: go to the ED immediately and do not wait for an OPD appointment.

title: Orthopedics and Sports Medicine Department
content: The Orthopedics department treats bones, joints, muscles, ligaments and the spine. Services: fracture care and casting; joint pain and arthritis management; knee, hip and shoulder replacement surgery; arthroscopy; spine consultation; sports injury treatment; pediatric orthopedics; and physiotherapy and rehabilitation. Bring previous X-rays, MRI reports, and prescriptions to the first visit. Physiotherapy sessions are 45 minutes and require a referral from a doctor; the number of sessions is decided by the physiotherapist. Urgent cases such as open fractures, severe trauma, or inability to move a limb after injury should go to the Emergency Department.

title: Gynecology and Obstetrics Department
content: The Gynecology and Obstetrics department provides care for women's health and pregnancy. Services: antenatal care and scans, normal and cesarean delivery, high-risk pregnancy care, postnatal care, family planning, infertility consultation, PCOS and menstrual disorders, menopause care, Pap smear, and gynecological surgery. Female doctors are available for consultation on request. Antenatal patients should bring previous records, ultrasound reports, and blood test results. Delivery packages (normal and cesarean) with room options are available; details and pricing are provided by the Maternity Billing Desk. Bleeding in pregnancy, severe abdominal pain, reduced baby movement, leaking fluid, or labour pain are emergencies and the patient should come directly to the Emergency Department or the Labour Room.

title: Pediatrics and Neonatology Department
content: The Pediatrics department provides care for newborns, infants, children and adolescents up to 16 years. Services: general child health consultation, vaccination clinic (EPI and additional vaccines), growth and development monitoring, nutrition counselling, asthma and allergy care, neonatal ICU (NICU), and pediatric emergency care. Parents should bring the child's vaccination card, birth certificate or B-Form, and previous records. Pediatric OPD is open from 9:00 AM to 9:00 PM, Monday to Saturday. High fever with drowsiness, fits, breathing difficulty, persistent vomiting or dehydration, or injury in a child should be taken to the Emergency Department immediately. The vaccination clinic works Monday to Saturday from 10:00 AM to 6:00 PM; booking is recommended.

title: Complaints, Feedback and Patient Support
content: Patients and families can share feedback or complaints through the Patient Relations Office (ground floor, open 9:00 AM to 8:00 PM), by phone on 051-111-555-000 extension 5, by email at feedback@rehmatmedical.example, or through the feedback form on the website. Complaints are acknowledged within 24 hours and the hospital aims to resolve them within 7 working days. Serious complaints involving patient safety are escalated to the Medical Director. Billing disputes should be raised with the Billing Department with the original invoice and receipts. The hospital also provides a patient advocate for elderly, disabled, and non-English or Urdu speaking patients. Feedback from patients is reviewed monthly by hospital management to improve services.

title: Limits of the AI Booking Assistant - What It Cannot Do
content: The hospital's AI booking assistant is designed to help with appointments, hospital information, policies, and general preparation guidance based on hospital documents. It cannot: diagnose conditions, recommend or change medicines or doses, interpret lab or scan results, confirm insurance coverage for a specific patient, give legal advice, or handle emergencies. If a question is not covered by hospital documents, the assistant should say it does not have that information and direct the patient to the right contact, such as the helpline 051-111-555-000, the Insurance Desk, or the Billing Department. For possible emergencies, the assistant must tell the patient to call 051-111-555-911, go to the Emergency Department, or call an ambulance service immediately. Patients with urgent symptoms should not wait for a booking confirmation.
